labeled_by: Claude (Fable 5) from materials-science first principles, BLIND to model output, pre-scoring
note: Sealed labels, written before any Q12 prediction was executed. Expert judgment, not external experimental ground truth; borderline pairs flagged. Independence caveat: authored by the same assistant that worked on the codebase.

12001.basis: NCA at ~3.8 V in ethylene carbonate is standard commercial Li-ion chemistry

12002.basis: LGPS oxidizes above ~2.5 V vs Li; a 3.8 V NCA cathode decomposes it without a coating

12003.basis: LATP is oxidation-stable to ~4.2 V so it can face an NMC811 cathode - BORDERLINE (interfacial resistance reported)

12004.basis: Si operates at 0.01-0.5 V, far below the ~2.4 V Ti(IV) reduction onset; LATP is reduced

12005.basis: Al is the standard collector used with sulfide solid electrolytes on the cathode side - BORDERLINE (some interfacial resistance reported)

12006.basis: Cu dissolves above ~3.2 V; it cannot serve as the collector for a 4 V-class LATP cathode side

12007.basis: PVDF dissolves in acetone; a standard PVDF casting solvent alongside NMP/DMF

12008.basis: Polypropylene is not soluble in NMP; it cannot be solution-cast from it

12009.basis: PEO is water-soluble and routinely processed from aqueous solution

12010.basis: PET is not water-soluble; aqueous solution processing is not possible

12011.basis: PA66 absorbs ~8% water with substantial dimensional and stiffness change

12012.basis: Polypropylene has negligible water uptake; standard for aqueous service

12013.basis: Both are high-Tg amorphous engineering thermoplastics but are not a known miscible pair - BORDERLINE

12014.basis: Polar PC and non-polar HDPE are strongly immiscible with negligible interfacial adhesion

12015.basis: Zn is anodic to brass and is sacrificially consumed - BORDERLINE (protects the brass, but the Zn part degrades)

12016.basis: Cu is strongly cathodic to carbon steel and drives rapid steel corrosion in seawater

12017.basis: Ni-Mo are mutually soluble and are joined in Ni-Mo alloy systems (Hastelloy family) - BORDERLINE

12018.basis: Al-Ti fusion welding forms brittle TiAl3 intermetallics

12019.basis: Kovar (~5.5 ppm/K) is designed to seal to borosilicate; the standard matched seal

12020.basis: Aluminium ~23 ppm/K against borosilicate 3.3 ppm/K; the seal cracks on cooling

12021.basis: Au interdiffuses into Bi2Te3 and degrades the contact without a barrier - BORDERLINE

12022.basis: Refractory Mo acts as a diffusion barrier to Bi2Te3 - BORDERLINE (less standard than Ni)

12023.basis: AlAs (5.66 A) on GaP (5.45 A) is ~3.8% mismatched; not coherently epitaxial

12024.basis: ZnSe (5.669 A) and Ge (5.658 A) are lattice matched to ~0.2%; a classic matched heteropair

12025.basis: Si3N4-TiN is a standard electroconductive ceramic composite; the phases coexist

12026.basis: SiC and MgO react/reduce at high temperature rather than coexisting inertly - BORDERLINE

12027.basis: PTFE's very low surface energy makes it immiscible with polar polyamides

12028.basis: Si3N4 and mullite have close CTE and are chemically compatible

12029.basis: HA coating on Ti6Al4V is the standard orthopaedic implant system

12030.basis: W metallization on alumina is the standard co-fired ceramic package system - BORDERLINE

12031.basis: Mg is extremely anodic to stainless steel; severe galvanic attack of the Mg

12032.basis: Tin is cathodic to steel, so a breach in tinplate accelerates steel corrosion - BORDERLINE

12033.basis: InN has a much larger lattice constant than AlGaN; the mismatch precludes coherent epitaxy

12034.basis: InP-matched InGaAs (5.87 A) against InAs (6.06 A) is ~3% mismatched - BORDERLINE

12035.basis: Soda-lime ~9 ppm/K vs borosilicate 3.3 ppm/K; direct sealing cracks

12036.basis: Both are thiophosphate sulfide electrolytes with compatible chemistry
